questions.prompt:
Complete the following:
The Internet of Everything (IoE) is a network connection of people, process, data and ........................... .
questions.markSchemeHint: Things.

questions.prompt: Identify two emergency services that could use the IoE.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two of: Police, Fire (and Rescue), Ambulance / Paramedics, Coastguard, Mountain Rescue.

questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using online surveys to collect information.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (1+1): reaches large audience quickly/cheaply, automatic data collation/analysis, convenient for respondents. Disadvantage (1+1): excludes people without internet access, low response rate, risk of dishonest/incomplete answers.

questions.scenarioContext: Online surveys can be used to collect information.
questions.prompt: Identify one other primary data collection method that could be used to collect information.
questions.markSchemeHint: Interviews, focus groups, paper questionnaires, observations, polls.

questions.scenarioContext: A computer game is being created to teach primary school pupils about road safety. Pupils will play the game by answering four questions about road safety. Each time they answer a question, the pupils will receive feedback about their answer. The game will be played using a website on a desktop computer.
questions.prompt: Explain how using a Human Computer Interface (HCI) on a website will impact the design of the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: must be compatible across different web browsers/screen resolutions, clear navigation/menu bar, suitable media sizes for fast loading over internet, designed for mouse/keyboard interaction on desktop.

questions.scenarioContext: Road safety educational game website for primary schools.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Purpose: flood the web server with excessive requests/traffic to exhaust bandwidth/resources and disrupt service. Impact: website slows down or crashes, pupils/schools cannot access the road safety game, loss of trust/reputation, cost/time for IT recovery. Logical prevention: firewalls/traffic filtering, intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS), rate limiting/load balancing, up-to-date anti-malware/patches.

questions.scenarioContext:
The road safety game is designed in the following way:
• When the game starts, pupils enter their name.
• A question then appears on the screen with a correct and incorrect answer. Pupils must select their answer.
• If they select the correct answer a point is added to their score.
• If they select the incorrect answer, an information message appears on the screen. The message disappears after five seconds.
• The next question appears.
• After four questions have been answered, the pupil's score is shown on the screen.
questions.prompt:
Create a flowchart for this process in the game.
Marks will be awarded for: layout; content.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Layout (correct standard OCR flowchart symbols: ovals for Start/Stop, parallelograms for Input/Output, rectangles for Processes, diamonds for Decisions with Yes/No arrows, clear directional flowlines) and up to 4 marks Content (Enter name -> Display question & input answer -> Decision: Correct? -> Yes: add 1 to score / No: display message & wait 5 seconds -> Loop check: 4 questions answered? -> Output final score -> Stop).

questions.scenarioContext: Road safety game where pupils answer four questions and receive a score.
questions.prompt: Identify the data type that will be used for the score at the end of the game. Justify your choice.
questions.markSchemeHint: Integer / Numeric (1 mark). Justification (2 marks): the score is a whole number (0 to 4) with no decimals/fractions, and numeric values allow arithmetic/incrementing points (+1) and comparisons.

questions.scenarioContext: Road safety game for primary school pupils.
questions.prompt: Explain how a presence check will be used to check that pupils have answered a question.
questions.markSchemeHint: Checks that an answer has been selected/entered and the field is not left blank (1) before allowing the pupil to submit or move to the next question, prompting an error message if empty (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A presence check checks that pupils have answered a question.
questions.prompt: Identify two other validation tools that are used to reduce errors.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: range check, length check, format check / input mask, data type check, lookup / limited choice (drop-down, radio buttons), check digit.

questions.scenarioContext: Schools storing pupil and game data on a network drive.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to schools of storing data on a network drive.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): centralised access from any school computer, easier central backups/security management, easy file sharing among teachers. Disadvantage (2): if the server/network goes down nobody can access files, hardware/maintenance cost, single point of failure/cyber-attack target.

questions.scenarioContext: A network drive can be accessed using a wired network.
questions.prompt: Explain two disadvantages to schools of using a wired network.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each (point + explanation): expensive/disruptive to install cables across classrooms; trip hazard/cable damage; devices lack mobility (fixed to wall sockets); limited number of ports for expansion.

questions.scenarioContext:
A pupil can use a microphone to enter data using their voice. At the end of the game the pupil's final score will be heard by the pupil and displayed on the screen.

Select missing IoE pillars from: Thing, People, Process (each pillar can be used more than once) and justify your selections.
questions.prompt: Complete Column 1, Column 2, and Column 3 in the table below.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 mark missing pillar + 2 marks justification): Input -> People (or Thing) + Data (pupil speaks answer into microphone creating voice data); Score -> Data + Process (software processes pupil's answers to calculate total score); Output -> Thing + People (desktop screen/speakers output the final score to the pupil).

questions.prompt: Identify two characteristics of Bluetooth connectivity.
questions.markSchemeHint: Short range (~10m), wireless radio waves, low power consumption, lower bandwidth/data transfer rate than Wi-Fi, easy device pairing, no internet needed.

questions.prompt: Identify the type of software that could be used to create an infographic.
questions.markSchemeHint: Desktop Publishing (DTP) software, graphics/image editing software, or presentation software.

questions.scenarioContext: An infographic has been created to advertise the road safety computer game to schools.
questions.prompt: Explain two advantages to schools of an infographic being used to advertise the game.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each (point + explanation): visually engaging/eye-catching so busy teachers notice it; summarises key facts/benefits quickly without dense text; easy to share digitally via email/websites or print for staffrooms.
